messages:
marta: quick idea — we should discuss a lightweight "delegation" mode for resident writes when the tenant's primary region is saturated. not a full failover, just a controlled delegation to a 'sanctuary' region for a small window.

sam: explain 'sanctuary' pls — is this another primary or a temporary proxy?

marta: temporary proxy + legal tag. we mark the request as delegated and carry provenance. main goals: avoid hard failovers, keep write success rate up during spikes, and keep auditable residency metadata.

kevin: sounds useful. major concerns: data residency/compliance. if a tenant is EU-resident we can't persist in us-east unless customer explicitly allows it. how do we ensure policy enforcement?

marta: we keep policy checks in the control plane. delegation only allowed if tenant has an explicit cross-region delegation policy or a pre-signed 'consent token'. otherwise we reject / return 409 with hint.

lia: operationally, how do we surface this to apps? I don't want app teams to change their retry logic. ideally it's transparent but with clear headers so downstream can audit.

sam: propose minimal API change: add optional response header `X-Delegated-Region: <region>` and `X-Delegation-Reason: quota|overload|maintenance`. No request changes required; client opt-in via `X-Allow-Delegation: true` if they can tolerate non-local persistence and consent.

kevin: governance: consent token solution sounds neat. control plane issues a signed JWT that includes allowed destination regions, TTL and policy id. runtime verifies signature before accepting delegation. keeps audit trail.

marta: exact. plus we log a delegation-event to customer audit stream. also emit telemetry: delegated_write_ratio per tenant, latency delta, and failback success rate.

lia: what about KV cache and session affinity? If we delegate writes elsewhere, reads from the original region may be stale. do we force read-throughs to sanctuary for a TTL?

sam: options: (1) sticky delegation: for a short `delegation_ttl` (e.g. 30s) route traffic to delegated region, and populate proxy cache with `delegated=true` flags; (2) prefix-KV bridging: piggyback cross-region cache fill for keys written under delegation; (3) conservative: return 202 and surface read inconsistency note.

kevin: option (1) is simplest for correctness but increases cross-region latency if most reads still hit origin. (2) is more complex but better UX. (3) is more explicit but forces app-level handling.

lia: prefer (1) for MVP with clear metrics. we can follow up with (2) as a performance refactor.

marta: agree. also need safe rollback: if sanctuary becomes primary accidentally we must ensure we don't create split-brain. delegation must be idempotent and always append to the same logical stream/tag.

sam: implement delegation as a write-side proxy that attaches a monotonic delegation-id and writes metadata: `delegation_id`, `delegated_from_region`, `consent_token_id`. on reconciliation, we can detect duplicates by delegation_id.

kevin: and what about read-after-write guarantees? if we route reads to origin by default, we should either (a) return a `stale=true` header until cross-region replication confirms, or (b) route reads to delegated region for keys touched under active delegation. both need schema to mark keys as "in-flight-delegation".

lia: add `X-Read-Safe-Until` in response maybe — gives client a timestamp when origin will be consistent. but we need to compute that safely.

marta: from infra side: the runtime needs a new small state machine: IDLE -> DELEGATING -> DELEGATED -> FAILBACK. operator-triggered or auto via overload metric. each transition emits events to control plane.

sam: interfaces: runtime->control-plane RPC `RequestDelegation(tenant, reason) -> {allowed:bool, destination_region, consent_token_id}`. keep it synchronous so we never delegate silently without policy.

kevin: make sure RequestDelegation is rate-limited and idempotent. also design for eventual offline decisions: if control plane unreachable, runtime must either fail open (not allowed) or fail closed. I vote fail closed for compliance.

lia: testing matrix: simulate traffic spike + delegate to EU->EU-satellite, verify audit logs, verify reads consistent for 30s TTL, verify metrics report. add chaos test on control-plane unavailability.

marta: rollout plan: feature-flagged in dedicated, then private. default off for hosted; customers can opt-in per tenant with consent token via console/API. docs + FAQ for legal.

sam: long-term refactor idea: make delegation decisions part of routing policy language so we can express: prefer_local, allow_delegate_if_consent, prefer_next_best_region, fallback_quorum. would let us reuse routing DSL for other modes.

kevin: yeah, unify with existing fallback DSL. but avoid coupling too much initially — deliver simple RPC contract first.

lia: small nit: include a metric `delegation_latency_p50/p95` so we know perf delta. also `delegation_consents_granted` for compliance ops.

marta: action items: 1) sam to draft runtime->control-plane RPC proto (this week). 2) kevin to sketch consent-token JWT fields + rotation policy. 3) lia to write MVP operator runbook + test cases. 4) infra-bot to add feature flag in config service.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-2481: "delegation: runtime control-plane contract + MVP" and flagged oncall. :white_check_mark:

sam: I'll start a short RFC doc with the proto and sequence diagram. thanks all.

kevin: one more: please include an explicit 'delegation_audit_id' header so analytics teams can correlate across regions.

marta: good call. we'll include `X-Delegation-Audit-Id`. we'll reconvene after RFC draft. :sparkles:
